beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — shared resource competition
beats.narration_text: The tumor microenvironment is a resource battlefield. Glucose, amino acids, oxygen — whatever the tumor needs, it takes. This plate shows what that looks like for an immune cell trying to function in the same space.

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — metabolic immune suppression
beats.narration_text: T-cells need glucose and arginine to proliferate and kill. Tumors consume both at rates normal tissue never approaches. The T-cell starves — not attacked, not suppressed by a checkpoint, just outcompeted. Metabolic immunotherapy tries to level the playing field.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_ImmuneStarvation class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The reservoir is one Rectangle — ORANGE outline, no fill, five dots near the bottom to show the tank is low. The thick pipe is a line with stroke width twenty-two; the thin pipe is stroke width five. The tumor cluster is seven BLUE circles in a VGroup; the immune cell is a single SKY circle with a VERM dashed stroke. The asymmetry is built into the geometry: thick versus thin is the whole argument.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_ImmuneStarvation
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"
ORANGE="#E69F00"; VERM="#D55E00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_ImmuneStarvation(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # reservoir — ORANGE outline, near-empty
    res=Rectangle(width=2.2,height=3.5,color=ORANGE)
    dots=[Dot(res.get_bottom()+UP*(0.3+i*0.22)+RIGHT*(-0.3+j*0.3),
              radius=0.1,color=ORANGE)
          for i,j in [(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1)]]
    # thick left pipe → tumor cluster
    thick=Line(ORIGIN,LEFT*2.5,color=GRAY,stroke_width=22)
    thick.next_to(res,LEFT,buff=0)
    cluster=VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.22,color=BLUE,
      fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.8)
      for _ in range(7)]).arrange_in_grid(3,3,buff=0.08)
    cluster.next_to(thick,LEFT,buff=0.1)
    # thin right pipe → lone immune cell
    thin=Line(ORIGIN,RIGHT*2.5,color=GRAY,stroke_width=5)
    thin.next_to(res,RIGHT,buff=0)
    immune=Circle(radius=0.35,color=VERM,
      fill_color=SKY,fill_opacity=0.18,
      stroke_width=3).next_to(thin,RIGHT,buff=0.1)
    immune.set_stroke(color=VERM,width=3)
    self.play(FadeIn(res),*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots])
    self.play(Create(thick),LaggedStart(
      *[FadeIn(c) for c in cluster],lag_ratio=0.12))
    self.play(Create(thin),FadeIn(immune))
    self.wait(0.8)
props.sparkLine: Thick vs thin — that's the argument.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_ImmuneStarvation — watch the asymmetric pipe geometry
beats.narration_text: Run it. The reservoir appears — nearly empty, five dots near the bottom. The thick pipe builds left, and the tumor cluster fades in, seven circles. Then the thin pipe builds right, and the lone immune cell appears — SKY fill, VERM dashed border. The geometry does the arguing: thick pipe, seven fed cells versus thin pipe, one starved cell.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: reservoir dots flow rapidly left to tumor cluster, LaggedStart toward seven circles — many dots. Tumor cluster grows scale one point one five as it consumes. One dot starts right toward immune cell, then fades — never arrives. Immune cell shrinks scale zero point eight five to show starvation. Reservoir visibly empties: remove dots from the bottom of the tank as they leave.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_ImmuneStarvationContrast — dots flow left, immune cell shrinks
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The reservoir dots animate left — LaggedStart, rapid, feeding the tumor. The tumor cluster scales up slightly as the nutrients arrive. One dot ventures right toward the immune cell — and fades before it gets there. The immune cell shrinks. The reservoir empties. That is metabolic immunosuppression — not a drug, not a checkpoint, just arithmetic.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: One pool, two drinkers, an asymmetric draw. The animation made the competition concrete: watch where the dots go, and you have understood metabolic immune suppression. Claude ported the plate geometry in one prompt and added the flow dynamics in one revision. The pattern — reservoir, directional pipes, dot animation — works for any shared-resource competition in the tumor microenvironment.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third competitor to the reservoir — a regulatory T-cell that also draws from the pool, but draws less than the tumor and more than the cytotoxic T-cell. Why run it? Because the tumor microenvironment is not a two-player game. Regulatory T-cells actively consume resources and suppress the immune response simultaneously. Adding a third pipe at intermediate thickness forces you to ask: where does the Treg sit in the hierarchy, and what does eliminating it actually free up for the cytotoxic cell trying to work beside it.

draws more than the cytotoxic T-cell but less than the tumor.
Show the three-way competition: thick pipe → tumor, medium pipe → Treg,
thin pipe → cytotoxic T-cell. Animate all three dot flows simultaneously."
